title: Why Do You See a GREEN Dot That Isn't There? 👁️
description:
Keep your eyes on the cross. A green dot seems to run round the ring, but there is no green on the screen. Staring at each blurry pink dot tires out the colour sensing in the patch of your eye it falls on. When the dot blinks off, that patch sees plain grey with the pink taken out: its opposite, green (a negative afterimage), and your brain joins the flashes into one dot racing round. Keep staring and the pink dots can fade away completely, because blurry things that never change stop being reported (Troxler fading, described in 1804). In the 1950s, scientists stuck a tiny picture onto people's eyeballs with a suction cap, so the picture moved with the eye and never changed on it; usually within a few seconds it faded away. Did the pink dots vanish? Yes or no?

The illusion is Jeremy Hinton's lilac chaser (2005).
